title: Real projection and inclusion for complex Bochner integrals
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be any measure space. If $h:X\to\mathbf C$ is Bochner integrable, then $\operatorname{Re}h:X\to\mathbf R$ is Bochner integrable and $$\int_X\operatorname{Re}h\,d\mu=\operatorname{Re}\left(\int_X h\,d\mu\right).$$ For every function $f:X\to\mathbf R$, with the Bochner integral set to zero when its integrand is not integrable, $$\int_X (f(x):\mathbf C)\,d\mu=\left(\int_X f\,d\mu:\mathbf C\right).$$ Bochner integrable means strongly measurable outside a null set and having finite integral of the norm; strongly measurable means a pointwise limit of measurable simple functions, whose images are finite and whose fibres are measurable.
